```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune"))$reference`
* Article: [CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2023;12(10):1450-1460](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13022)
  (open access, PMC10583246). The model equations and the authors' nlmixr
  estimation and simulation code are in Supplementary material S1 and S2.

Zhang et al. compared eight within-host viral dynamic models for SARS-CoV-2
(slope-intercept, target-cell-limited (TCL), reduced TCL, TCL with an eclipse
phase (TCLE), and four TCLE variants with an immune-response compartment) on
daily upper-respiratory-tract viral loads from a UK community cohort followed
from contact with an infectious case. The best model by BIC (Table 2, M7) is a
TCLE model in which an immune response `F`, produced by productively infected
cells, increases viral clearance through a saturable term
`phi * F / (F + theta)`. Only M7 has published parameter estimates; the other
seven structures are reported by BIC alone and are not reproducible.

The paper contributes two models to nlmixr2lib:

| Model | Fit | Used here for |
|-------|-----|---------------|
| `Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune` | M7 on all 162 patients, `c` and `k` fixed (Table 3) | Figure 3 (timing and efficacy of an entry-blocking antiviral) |
| `Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune_age` | M7 with age on `delta`, fitted to unvaccinated patients (Supplement S2 simulation code) | Figure 4 (tixagevimab-cilgavimab phase III trial) |

```{r models}
mod_all <- readModelDb("Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune")
mod_age <- readModelDb("Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune_age")
```

Both models are expressed in days since contact. The antiviral effect is the
paper's blockade of de novo infection (Eq. 3-7): `beta` is multiplied by
`1 - eta * H(t)` with `H(t) = 1` from the treatment start `t*` onward. In the
model files `eta` is `imax_beta` and `t*` is `t_intervention`; both default to
no treatment and can be set per subject by adding columns of the same name to
the event table.

# Population

The ATACCC study (Assessment of Transmission and Contagiousness of COVID-19 in
Contacts) recruited household and non-household contacts within 5 days of the
index case's symptom onset and swabbed them daily. The analysis dataset has
2155 viral loads from 162 patients (Table 1): ages 7-78 years (median 36),
124 household and 38 non-household contacts, 114 unvaccinated, 10 partially and
38 fully vaccinated, and pre-alpha (50), alpha (42) and delta (70) variants. No
patient received antiviral treatment. ORF1ab Ct values were converted to
copies/mL with Eq. 1, and Ct = 40 (31 copies/mL) was the limit of detection.
Time zero is the contact with the infectious case; for household contacts it
was imputed as 7 days before the viral-load peak.

The age-covariate model was fitted to the unvaccinated patients: the Methods
state that the simulation parameters came from "the model that was fitted to
unvaccinated patients", and the BICs of the covariate models in Supplement S5
(about 7880) are on a smaller dataset than the all-patient base model (12182).

```{r population}
str(mod_all()$population[c("species", "n_subjects", "n_observations", "disease_state")])
str(mod_age()$population[c("n_subjects", "notes")])
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | `..._tcle_immune` | `..._tcle_immune_age` | Source location |
|----------------------|-------------------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| `dT/dt = -beta V T` | yes | yes | Supplement S1 (M7); Eq. 3 |
| `dI1/dt = beta V T - k I1` | yes | yes | Supplement S1 (M7); Eq. 4 |
| `dI2/dt = k I1 - delta I2` | yes | yes | Supplement S1 (M7); Eq. 5 |
| `dV/dt = rho I2 - c V - phi F/(F+theta) V - beta V T` | yes | yes | Supplement S1 (M7); Eq. 6 |
| `dF/dt = I2 - dF F` | yes | yes | Supplement S1 (M7); Eq. 7 |
| `T(0) = T0, I1(0) = 0, I2(0) = 1/30, V(0) = V0, F(0) = 0` | yes | yes | Methods 'Assumptions on parameters'; Supplement S2 |
| Antiviral `beta * (1 - eta H(t))` | yes | yes | Methods 'Simulations for antiviral therapies', Eq. 3-6 |
| `R0` | 13.74 (`beta` derived) | derived output | Table 3; Results 'Parameter estimation' (definition) |
| `beta` | from `R0` | exp(-14.654) = 4.33e-7 | Supplement S2 simulation code `tbeta` |
| `delta` (1/day) | 1.04 | exp(-0.0242) = 0.976 at 35 y | Table 3; Supplement S2 `tdelta` |
| `phi` (1/day) | 0.24 | exp(-1.549) = 0.212 | Table 3; Supplement S2 `tphi` |
| `theta` | 542.46 | exp(6.281) = 534 | Table 3; Supplement S2 `ttheta` |
| `V0` (copies/mL) | 23.33 | exp(3.193) = 24.4 | Table 3; Supplement S2 `tv0` |
| Age on `delta` | none | `(AGE/35)^-0.11` | Supplement S2 simulation code |
| `rho` (copies/cell/day) | 6000 fixed | 6000 fixed | Table 3 |
| `c` (1/day) | 20 fixed | 20 fixed | Table 3 |
| `k` (1/day) | 3 fixed | 3 fixed | Table 3 |
| `dF` (1/day) | 0.4 fixed | 0.4 fixed | Table 3; Methods |
| `T0` (cells/mL) | 1.33e5 fixed | 1.33e5 fixed | Table 3; Methods |
| IIV variance on `beta`, `delta`, `V0`, `phi`, `theta` | 0.01 each | 0.01 each | Supplement S2 simulation code (`ombeta` ... `omtheta`) |
| Residual SD | 3 (ln) = 1.303 (log10) | 3 (ln) = 1.303 (log10) | Eq. 2; Supplement S2 simulation code (`sd = 3`) |

# Deterministic checks

## R0 and the derived infection rate

The all-patient model is parameterised by the published basic reproductive
number. With `F(0) = 0` the paper's definition reduces to
`R0 = rho beta T0 / (delta (c + beta T0))`, which the model inverts for `beta`.
Recomputing `R0` from the solved `beta` must return the Table 3 value.

```{r r0-check}
ev0 <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 28, by = 0.05), evid = 0L, AGE = 35)
typ_all <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune")),
  events = ev0, returnType = "data.frame"
)
typ_age <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune_age")),
  events = ev0, returnType = "data.frame"
)
r0_back <- with(typ_all[1, ], rho * beta * T0 / (delta * (c + beta * T0)))
c(beta_all = typ_all$beta[1], R0_all = r0_back, beta_age = typ_age$beta[1], R0_age_35y = typ_age$R0[1])
stopifnot(abs(r0_back / 13.74 - 1) < 1e-8)
```

The age model's `R0` at 35 years (about 17.6) is higher than the all-patient
13.74, consistent with the higher `beta` of the unvaccinated fit. The Results
text quotes `R0 = 13.36` in one sentence and 13.74 in Table 3 and the
Discussion; the model uses the tabulated 13.74.

## Untreated trajectory

```{r untreated}
lod <- 133.3333 * exp((37.933 - 40) / 1.418) # Eq. 1 at Ct = 40
untreated <- bind_rows(
  typ_all |> mutate(model = "all patients (Table 3)"),
  typ_age |> mutate(model = "unvaccinated, age 35 y")
)
peaks <- untreated |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    tpeak = time[which.max(virus)],
    peak = max(virus),
    vl_day28 = virus[time == 28],
    f_target_day28 = f_target[time == 28],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(peaks, digits = c(0, 2, 0, 1, 6), caption = "Typical untreated trajectories.")
stopifnot(
  all(peaks$tpeak > 3 & peaks$tpeak < 5),
  all(peaks$peak > 1e7 & peaks$peak < 3e7),
  all(peaks$vl_day28 < lod)
)
```

Both typical trajectories peak near day 4 at about 2 x 10^7 copies/mL, as in
Figure 3a, and fall below the limit of detection (`r signif(lod, 3)` copies/mL)
before day 28, the end of the paper's simulation window.

```{r untreated-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(untreated, aes(time, virus, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = lod, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time since contact (days)", y = "Viral load (copies/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Figure 3: timing and efficacy of an entry-blocking antiviral

The authors' simulation script (Supplement S2) simulates 112 subjects aged 18
to 78 years with the IIV listed above, starts treatment on day 1, 4 or 7 after
contact with efficacy 0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9 or 0.99, and plots the mean viral load
and the mean fraction of target cells still uninfected on a daily grid. Two
details of the script matter for the comparison:

* the treatment indicator is linearly interpolated from 0 at `t*` to 1 at
  `t* + 1` (`approxfun()`), whereas Eq. 3-6 write a step at `t*`; the model
  files implement the equation. The ramp is reproduced below by supplying
  `imax_beta` as a time-varying event-table column, so both versions are shown;
* Figure 3 is reproduced by the all-patient (Table 3) parameters. The values
  coded in the script's defaults belong to the age model and do not reproduce
  it (see Assumptions and deviations).

```{r fig3-sim}
ages <- c(rep(18:65, 2), 65:75, 75, 75, 76, 77, 78) # Supplement S2 'Sims'
stopifnot(length(ages) == 112L)
scen <- tidyr::expand_grid(t_start = c(1, 4, 7), eff = c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 0.99)) |>
  mutate(scenario = row_number())

make_fig3_events <- function(t_start, eff, scenario, ramp) {
  ids <- (scenario - 1L) * length(ages) + seq_along(ages)
  times <- sort(unique(c(0:28, seq(t_start, t_start + 1, by = 0.05))))
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = times) |>
    mutate(
      evid = 0L,
      AGE = ages[id - (scenario - 1L) * length(ages)],
      t_intervention = if (ramp) 0 else t_start,
      imax_beta = if (ramp) eff * pmin(pmax(time - t_start, 0), 1) else eff,
      t_start = t_start, eff = eff, scenario = scenario
    )
}
simulate_fig3 <- function(ramp) {
  ev <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
    make_fig3_events(scen$t_start[i], scen$eff[i], scen$scenario[i], ramp = ramp)
  }) |>
    bind_rows()
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev[, c("id", "time")]))
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231001)
  rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb("Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune"),
    events = ev, keep = c("t_start", "eff", "scenario"),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |>
    filter(time %in% 0:28) |>
    group_by(t_start, eff, time) |>
    summarise(virus = mean(virus), f_target = mean(f_target), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(indicator = if (ramp) "1-day ramp (authors' script)" else "step at t* (Eq. 3-6)")
}
fig3 <- bind_rows(simulate_fig3(ramp = TRUE), simulate_fig3(ramp = FALSE))
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
fig3_long <- fig3 |>
  mutate(
    start = paste("treatment from day", t_start),
    efficacy = factor(eff)
  )
ggplot(fig3_long, aes(time, virus, colour = efficacy, linetype = indicator)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = lod, colour = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~start) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since contact (days)", y = "Mean viral load (copies/mL)",
    colour = "Efficacy", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3a-c of Zhang 2023."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
ggplot(fig3_long, aes(time, f_target, colour = efficacy, linetype = indicator)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~start) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since contact (days)", y = "Target cell ratio",
    colour = "Efficacy", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3d-f of Zhang 2023."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

The Results quote the outcome of four of these scenarios. The viral-load AUC
is the trapezoidal integral of the mean daily viral load from day 0 to 28.

```{r fig3-claims}
fig3_auc <- fig3 |>
  group_by(indicator, t_start, eff) |>
  summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(virus, -1) + tail(virus, -1)) / 2),
    f28 = f_target[time == 28],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(indicator, t_start) |>
  mutate(auc_reduction_pct = 100 * (1 - auc / auc[eff == 0])) |>
  ungroup()
claim_value <- function(ind, ts, e, col) {
  v <- fig3_auc[[col]][fig3_auc$indicator == ind & fig3_auc$t_start == ts & fig3_auc$eff == e]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique scenario row")
  v
}
ramp <- "1-day ramp (authors' script)"
step <- "step at t* (Eq. 3-6)"
claims <- tibble::tribble(
  ~claim, ~published, ~ind, ~ts, ~e, ~col,
  "Control viral-load AUC (copies*day/mL)", 3.9e7, ramp, 4, 0, "auc",
  "90% from day 1: AUC reduction (%)", 69.9, ramp, 1, 0.9, "auc_reduction_pct",
  "90% from day 1: target cells uninfected at day 28 (%)", 69.35, ramp, 1, 0.9, "f28",
  "90% from day 4: viral-load AUC (copies*day/mL)", 3.7e7, ramp, 4, 0.9, "auc",
  "90% from day 4: target cells uninfected at day 28 (%)", 0.4, ramp, 4, 0.9, "f28"
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    scale = if (col == "f28") 100 else 1,
    ramp_value = claim_value(ind, ts, e, col) * scale,
    step_value = claim_value(step, ts, e, col) * scale
  ) |>
  ungroup()
claims |>
  select(claim, published, ramp_value, step_value) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Results statement" = claim, "Published" = published,
    "Simulated, 1-day ramp" = ramp_value, "Simulated, step" = step_value
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

```{r fig3-gate}
auc_ctrl <- claim_value(ramp, 4, 0, "auc")
# Untreated AUC is cohort-insensitive (IIV variances 0.01): a mis-transcribed
# R0, delta, phi or theta moves it by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(auc_ctrl / 3.9e7 - 1) < 0.15)
# 99% efficacy from day 1 suppresses the infection; starting on day 4 or 7,
# after the target cells are depleted, changes the AUC by little (Results).
stopifnot(
  claim_value(ramp, 1, 0.99, "auc_reduction_pct") > 95,
  all(abs(fig3_auc$auc_reduction_pct[fig3_auc$t_start == 7]) < 5),
  all(abs(fig3_auc$auc_reduction_pct[fig3_auc$t_start == 4 & fig3_auc$indicator == ramp]) < 10)
)
# 90% from day 1 sits close to the R0 = 1 threshold, so the cohort mean is
# sensitive to the IIV draw; assert the paper's partial-protection regime
# (69.9% reduction) rather than a tight value.
stopifnot(
  claim_value(ramp, 1, 0.9, "auc_reduction_pct") > 40,
  claim_value(ramp, 1, 0.9, "auc_reduction_pct") < 90
)
```

With the authors' 1-day ramp the simulation reproduces the Results: the
untreated AUC, the near-complete protection at 99%, partial protection at 90%
started on day 1, and almost no benefit when treatment starts on day 4 or
later. The step of Eq. 3-6 acts half a day earlier on average and is therefore
somewhat more protective at 90% from day 1.

## Figure 3g-h: efficacy by initiation time

A typical-value version of the heat maps, on the step indicator of Eq. 3-6.

```{r fig3-heatmap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5}
grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(t_start = 0:10, eff = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = grid$id, time = seq(0, 28, by = 0.25)) |>
  left_join(grid, by = "id") |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, t_intervention = t_start, imax_beta = eff)
heat <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb("Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune")),
  events = ev_grid, keep = c("t_start", "eff"), returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  group_by(t_start, eff) |>
  summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(virus, -1) + tail(virus, -1)) / 2),
    f28 = f_target[time == 28], .groups = "drop"
  )
p_auc <- ggplot(heat, aes(t_start, eff, fill = auc)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue4") +
  labs(x = "Initiation of therapy (days since contact)", y = "Antiviral effect", fill = "AUC")
p_f <- ggplot(heat, aes(t_start, eff, fill = f28)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "firebrick", high = "white") +
  labs(x = "Initiation of therapy (days since contact)", y = "Antiviral effect", fill = "f")
p_auc
p_f
```

As in Figure 3g-h, a clear benefit is confined to efficacy above about 80%
started within about 3 days of contact.

# Figure 4: tixagevimab-cilgavimab phase III trial

Figure 4a simulates 112 patients per arm with the age model, treatment
efficacy 99%, and plots the mean and SD of log10 viral load at 0, 3, 6, 15 and
24 days after dosing, with a limit of quantification of 3.384 log10 copies/mL.
The paper does not state the treatment start relative to contact. Here dosing
is placed at the time the typical untreated log10 viral load first reaches
5.77, the mean value the Results report at treatment initiation. Values below
the limit of quantification are plotted at half the limit, matching the
plateau near 3.08 log10 copies/mL in both panels of Figure 4.

```{r fig4-sim}
loq <- 3.384
t_dose <- typ_age$time[which(log10(typ_age$virus) >= 5.77)[1]]
t_dose
obs_days <- c(0, 3, 6, 15, 24)
make_arm <- function(eff, id_offset) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = id_offset + seq_along(ages), time = t_dose + obs_days) |>
    mutate(
      evid = 0L,
      AGE = ages[id - id_offset],
      imax_beta = eff,
      t_intervention = t_dose,
      arm = if (eff > 0) "tixagevimab-cilgavimab" else "placebo"
    )
}
ev4 <- bind_rows(make_arm(0.99, 0L), make_arm(0, 112L))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev4[, c("id", "time")]))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231002)
sim4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_age,
  events = ev4, keep = c("arm"), returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(
    day = round(time - t_dose),
    vl = ifelse(sim < loq, loq - log10(2), sim)
  )
fig4 <- sim4 |>
  group_by(arm, day) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(vl), sd = sd(vl), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(fig4, digits = 2)
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(fig4, aes(day, mean, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd), width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = loq, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(placebo = "red3", "tixagevimab-cilgavimab" = "blue3")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 8)) +
  labs(
    x = "Days post dosing", y = "Log10 viral RNA (mean +/- SD)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4a of Zhang 2023."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig4-gate}
m4 <- function(a, d) fig4$mean[fig4$arm == a & fig4$day == d]
stopifnot(
  # Both arms start near the reported 5.77 log10 copies/mL (the dosing time is
  # anchored on the typical curve, so this checks the cohort around it).
  abs(m4("placebo", 0) - 5.77) < 0.6,
  abs(m4("tixagevimab-cilgavimab", 0) - 5.77) < 0.6,
  # Treatment lowers the mean viral load during the first week (Figure 4a:
  # about 0.9 log10 at day 3 and 0.8 at day 6).
  m4("placebo", 6) - m4("tixagevimab-cilgavimab", 6) > 0.3,
  # Both arms are below the limit of quantification by day 15 (Results: by
  # 12.7 days).
  m4("placebo", 15) < loq,
  m4("tixagevimab-cilgavimab", 15) < loq
)
```

The simulated arms start near 5.8 log10 copies/mL with an SD of 1.1-1.4
log10, close to the spread shown at day 0 of Figure 4a (about 1.4 to 1.6),
which supports the script's residual SD of 3 on the natural-log scale. The placebo arm rises to its peak
within the first days while the treated arm falls, and both reach the limit of
quantification before day 15.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV and residual error.** Neither is reported in the paper. Both models use
  the values in the authors' simulation script (Supplement S2): variance 0.01
  on `beta`, `delta`, `V0`, `phi` and `theta`, and residual SD 3 on the
  natural-log viral load (`exp(rnorm(mean = log(pred), sd = 3))`), stored as
  3 / log(10) = 1.303 on the log10 scale of the `log10_viral_load` output. The
  IIV values equal the initial values in the estimation code, so they may not
  be the final estimates. The day-0 spread of Figure 4a is consistent with the
  residual SD.
* **beta in the all-patient model.** Table 3 reports `R0` rather than `beta`.
  `beta` is solved from the paper's `R0` definition with `F(0) = 0`; IIV is
  applied to `beta`, as in the authors' code, not to `R0`. The eta keeps the
  name `etalbeta` (matching the age model) even though this file has no
  `lbeta` fixed effect, which the naming-convention check reports as a
  warning.
* **Age model values.** The parameters of the age-on-`delta` model are not
  tabulated in the paper. They are the "from NM" values coded in the
  Supplement S2 simulation script (`tbeta`, `tdelta`, `tv0`, `tphi`, `ttheta`,
  age exponent -0.11 on `log(age / 35)`). The fit's population (the 114
  unvaccinated patients) is inferred from the Methods and the Supplement S5
  BICs.
* **Which parameters generated Figure 3.** The script's default (age-model)
  values give a smaller benefit than the Results report for 90% efficacy from
  day 1 (about 27% AUC reduction against 69.9%), and peak timings that do not
  match Figure 3a, whereas the Table 3 values reproduce both. Figure 3 is
  therefore validated against `Zhang_2023_covid19_tcle_immune`, and the age
  model against Figure 4, the simulation the Methods tie to the unvaccinated
  fit.
* **Treatment indicator.** The model files implement the step `H(t)` of Eq.
  3-6. The authors' script ramps the indicator linearly over the day after
  `t*`; the vignette reproduces that ramp through a time-varying `imax_beta`
  column. The ramp reproduces the Results numbers more closely than the step.
* **Figure legend.** The Figure 3 caption lists efficacies of 99%, 95%, 80%
  and 50%, but its panels and the script use 0.99, 0.9, 0.8 and 0.5; the
  vignette uses the panel values.
* **Figure 4 dosing time.** Not reported; anchored on the reported mean viral
  load at treatment initiation (5.77 log10 copies/mL) as described above.
  Ages 18-78 follow the script's simulated population.
* **Units of `phi`.** Table 3 gives no unit; `phi` multiplies the viral load in
  `dV/dt`, so it is a rate (1/day). The immune response `F` and `theta` are in
  arbitrary units because `F` is produced at unit rate by productively infected
  cells.
* **Other model structures.** M1-M6 and M8 are reported by BIC only (Table 2),
  with no parameter estimates, and are not included. The Table 3 fit with `c`
  and `k` estimated (BIC 12,328) is a sensitivity analysis and is not included.
* **Covariates.** Vaccination status, contact type, variant and symptomatic
  status were screened graphically and not retained; only age entered the
  final model.
* No correction notice for this article was found in PubMed (checked
  2026-10-27).
